title: TORINO: Token Reduction via Interpretable Concept Overlap in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2607.04593v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities across different tasks, but their computational cost is dominated by the large number of visual tokens fed to the language model. Existing token reduction methods rely on attention-based scores or pairwise similarity, without an explicit semantic representation of each token. We introduce TORINO (TOken Reduction via Interpretable coNcept Overlap), a plug-and-play framework for adaptive visual token reduction in VLMs that requires no fine-tuning of the underlying model. TORINO leverages Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) to project visual tokens into an interpretable latent space where token relationships can be analyzed through shared concept activations. Specifically, we define concept overlap as the degree of agreement between active SAE latents and use it to group tokens that share semantic content. Reduction within each group is then performed by either pruning

translated_title: TORINO：通过可解释概念重叠实现视觉-语言模型中的词元削减
translated_abstract: 视觉-语言模型在各种任务中展现出了令人印象深刻的能力，但其计算成本主要由输入语言模型的大量视觉词元所主导。现有的词元削减方法依赖于基于注意力的评分或成对相似度，缺乏对每个词元的显式语义表示。我们提出了TORINO（TOken Reduction via Interpretable coNcept Overlap，通过可解释概念重叠进行词元削减），这是一个用于视觉-语言模型中自适应视觉词元削减的即插即用框架，无需对底层模型进行微调。TORINO利用稀疏自编码器将视觉词元投影到一个可解释的潜在空间中，在该空间中可以通过共享的概念激活来分析词元之间的关系。具体而言，我们将概念重叠定义为活跃SAE潜在特征之间的一致程度，并利用它对共享语义内容的词元进行分组，然后在每个组内通过剪枝等方式执行词元削减（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 提出即插即用框架TORINO，利用稀疏自编码器将视觉词元映射到可解释的潜在空间，基于概念重叠程度对词元分组并削减冗余词元，无需微调即可降低视觉-语言模型的计算成本。
en_tdlr: TORINO is a plug-and-play, fine-tuning-free framework that leverages sparse autoencoders to project visual tokens into an interpretable latent space and reduces tokens by grouping them according to concept overlap, thereby lowering the computational cost of vision-language models.
